conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—EPDS for short. It simply helps us pick up on signs of depression or anxiety that can creep up in the first months postpartum, and it includes one question about thoughts of self-harm so we can keep you safe.

Everything you share stays between us unless you give permission otherwise or if safety is a concern. There are just 10 questions, and we’ll talk through them together—no right or wrong answers, just whatever feels true for you lately.

Ready to begin? Here’s the first one:

Over the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… I can still laugh, but it doesn’t come as easily. I’d say I’ve managed to chuckle maybe a couple of times when my partner made a silly joke, but it feels kind of forced. I guess I’d say “not so much lately.”
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… I can still find things funny sometimes, but it’s like the laugh doesn’t last or feel as real as it used to. Mostly I’m just tired or thinking about the baby, so even when something’s amusing, it’s kind of flat.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Hmm… I do look forward to little things—like when my mom brings over dinner or when I get to take a short walk—but it’s not the same excitement I had before. It’s more like “okay, that’ll be nice,” rather than really feeling pumped up.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times this week I’ve caught myself thinking it’s my fault if she’s fussy or won’t nap—like maybe I’m missing some cue or not doing something right. I know rationally babies just cry, but in the moment I still hear that little voice saying, “You should’ve figured it out by now.”
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes, yeah. Like last night she was breathing a little fast while sleeping, and my mind jumped straight to “What if something’s wrong?” even though she was fine. I calmed myself down pretty quick, but these little worries pop up out of nowhere a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panic, but I do get these sudden little surges of “what-if” that make my heart race—like when I’m walking down the stairs with her and picture myself slipping. It passes in seconds, and I can talk myself down, so it’s more a quick scare than a real meltdown.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. It feels like as soon as I finish one feed, the laundry pile or the dishes is staring at me, and I think, “How am I supposed to keep up with all this?” I usually manage to muddle through, but it’s stressful and I end the day feeling kind of defeated.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I’ve had a little trouble drifting off a couple nights because my mind keeps running through the next day’s to-dos, but once I’m asleep I stay out. It’s more restlessness than being truly unhappy or weepy in the middle of the night.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel kind of down some days—like yesterday I just sat on the couch staring out the window while she napped, feeling blah. It’s not all day, but those waves of sadness hit maybe every other day, and then they lift after an hour or so.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, that happened twice this week—once when she wouldn’t latch and I felt stuck, and once when my partner asked how I was doing and I just teared up. It wasn’t sobbing all day, but the tears came and I couldn’t really stop them for a few minutes.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed and tired, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother (infant age not specified)  
Date: [today]

Presenting concerns endorsed (self-report):
- Diminished enjoyment/pleasure in daily activities; mood described as “flat” or “blah”  
- Intermittent tearfulness (2 crying episodes this week)  
- Mild depressive dips occurring “every other day,” lasting ~1 hour  
- Self-blame and guilt regarding infant care (“should’ve figured it out”)  
- Recurrent, intrusive “what-if” worries and brief surges of panic (no full panic attacks)  
- Feeling overwhelmed by routine tasks; end-of-day sense of defeat  
- Mild initial insomnia related to mental over-activity; sleep otherwise preserved  
- Persistent fatigue  
- Denies any self-harm ideation

Pattern: Sub-syndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms of mild-moderate intensity, with intact reality testing and no safety concerns. Symptoms interfere with emotional coping but do not appear to prevent basic infant care.

Screening significance: Meets partial criteria for **Unspecified Depressive Disorder and/or Unspecified Anxiety Disorder**, postpartum onset to be considered. Monitor for progression to Major Depressive Episode or Generalized Anxiety Disorder.

Risk factors noted:
- Postpartum status  
- Guilt/self-criticism  
- Anxiety amplification (health/safety of infant)  
- Social supports present (partner, mother) – protective

Plan: Continue monitoring; consider standardized follow-up (EPDS, PHQ-9/GAD-7) in 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen, persistent crying, or any thoughts of self-harm emerge.
